simple.meaning: מְעוּנִי (Mᵉʻûwnîy) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with flocks and in connection with kingship.

firstOccurrence.englishText: These written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and struck their tents. The Meunim who were found there, and they destroyed them utterly to this day, and lived in their place; because there was pasture there for their flocks.

definitions.full: H4586. Meunim or Meinim מְעוּנִים proper name, of a people Me`unim, Me`unites (usually connected with מָעוֺן , (see עון ), but dubious, compare Buhl Edom. 41 f. ); — a people South (SE ?) of Canaan (compare Buhl l.c .); — ׳הַמּ 2Chr 26:7 and 1Chr 4:41 Qr (Kt ᵐ5 המעינים, B τοὺς Μιναίους , ᵐ5 L τ. Κιναίους ; read also מֵהַמְּעוּנִים 2Chr 20:1 (for מֵהָעַמּוֺנִים ᵑ0 ), so ᵐ5 B A ( ᵐ5 L Αμμανιειμ ), Ew Be Ke Ot Kau Kit; בְּנֵימְֿעוּנִים (among Nethinim who went back with Zerubbabel) Ezra 2:50 = Neh 7:52 are perhaps descendants of those named above ( 2Chr 26:7 ). ᵐ5 οἱ Μιναῖοι , but against ׳מ = Mineans (Glaser Skizze ii. 450 f. and others) see Sprenger ZMG xliv (1890), 505 . [ מָעוּף ] see עיף . מָעוֺר see עור . מעז (√ of following). מעינים 1Chr 4:41 Kt see מְעוּנִים .
